final_diagnosis.root_cause: The ts-order-service Deployment in namespace train-ticket has been scaled to 0 replicas, leaving its Service with no Endpoints. All traffic to ts-order-service routes (and downstream flows depending on it) consequently fails with 503/500 errors.
final_diagnosis.report:
The ts-order-service Deployment in namespace train-ticket has been scaled to 0 replicas, leaving its Service with no Endpoints

## Findings
• Deployment ts-order-service is at 0/0 replicas in namespace train-ticket.
• Service ts-order-service has zero endpoints and TCP connectivity to it fails.
• A ScalingReplicaSet event scaled ts-order-service from 1 to 0 ~4m56s before the snapshot, followed by pod deletion and container Killing events.
• The application manifest (GetAppYAML) specifies replicas: 1, so live state is drifted from declared state.
• 503 alerts target routes entering ts-order-service; 500s on the preserve flow occur on a path whose dependency chain traverses ts-order-service.
• All 4 nodes are Ready, kube-scheduler is healthy, MySQL (tsdb-mysql-0/1/2) and other ts-* deployments are 1/1 Running, ruling out infrastructure/database causes.

*Non-Validated Claims (Inferred):*
• The actor or mechanism that triggered the scale-down (manual kubectl scale, HPA with minReplicas 0, GitOps overlay, etc.) is unknown from the available tools.
• Whether the 21 preserve-flow 500s are entirely cascade failures from ts-order-service or partially due to in-flight transaction side effects is not fully confirmed.
• No application logs for ts-order-service were retrievable (no pods exist), so no in-process error signal corroborates the cascade hypothesis.

## Recommended Actions
• Immediately restore replicas: kubectl -n train-ticket scale deployment/ts-order-service --replicas=1 and wait for the pod to become Ready (TCP readinessProbe on 12031 with 60s initial delay).
• Verify recovery: kubectl -n train-ticket get endpoints ts-order-service shows a populated endpoint, and rerun CheckServiceConnectivity against the correct Service port 12031 (also reconcile any alert probe still targeting port 80).
• Re-apply the source-of-truth manifest from Git (kubectl apply -f ts-order-service.yaml) to prevent drift back to 0 replicas.
• Audit the cause: review kubectl events sorted by lastTimestamp, check for an HPA (kubectl -n train-ticket get hpa) with minReplicas=0 and raise to >=1, and inspect Argo/Flux or audit logs for the scale-down actor.
• Add guardrails: a PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable: 1 for ts-order-service and an alert on kube_deployment_spec_replicas == 0 for production deployments.
• After ts-order-service is healthy, confirm 500/503 alert counters stop incrementing and review ts-preserve-service and ts-gateway-service logs for any retry-storm fallout.


*Cited Evidence:*
- Queries: CheckNodeServiceStatus, CheckServiceConnectivity, DescribeResource, GetAlerts, GetAppYAML, GetClusterConfiguration, GetErrorLogs, GetRecentLogs, GetResources, GetServiceDependencies, describe eks addon, describe eks cluster, get eks events, get eks node health, get eks nodegroup health, list eks clusters, list eks deployments, list eks namespaces, list eks pods
